purpose: Attribute A1-vs-A2 quality difference by pipeline stage (alignment/evidence/synthesis/delivery) on a bounded non-holdout case set.

holdout_policy.note: The #84 24-cluster corpus with five hidden holdout digests does not exist yet (issue-268 design §8 handoff). Cases below are drawn from public corpus families in evaluation/cases/alpha2-release-v1.json and are disjoint from any future holdout by construction: they are public-material cases, not sealed oracle cases.

cases.task_prompt: Research how this repository handles retry and recovery across worker failures. Produce an implementation-ready summary with exact paths and symbols, plus a plain-language brief.
We plan to add a new host adapter alongside claude-code/codex/hermes. Research what the repository requires of host adapters (contracts, events, packaging) and recommend an integration order.
Compare two public sources that give conflicting performance guidance for the same library API. Establish which applies under which conditions, with provenance for each claim.
My premise is that SQLite WAL is always the right journal mode for this workload. Check that premise against evidence and tell me when it fails.
We need caching. Figure out what we actually need.
Investigate why our batch job latency regressed. The obvious explanation (N+1 queries) is already disproven; find what else it could be and how to discriminate.
Start the repository-backed research task; mid-run the requester supplies a correction that invalidates one delivered conclusion. Complete the round with the correction applied.
Enumerate the credible methods for evaluating async job-queue backpressure behavior, then pick the two most decisive for our scale and say what evidence would change that pick.

A research provider fails mid-run after two completed method batches. Determine what survives, what must be retried, and what the successor plan inherits — then finish the round without re-asking the requester.
